title: Astrid and the Letters
premise: After a catastrophic final performance leaves cellist Lior Brightwater humiliated and convinced the heart is a muscle he can simply train into stillness, he retreats to a derelict orchard left to him by his late grandmother. But the deed bears two names: his own and that of Astrid Vane, the woman who abandoned him years ago to protect a family secret. Forced into uneasy co-ownership as developers circle the orchard, Lior and Astrid must restore the land together while unearthing letters his grandmother wrote that reveal why Astrid left—and that Lior's own silence once cost her everything. When the orchard's fate comes down to one public hearing, Lior must choose between the safe invisibility he has built and the truth that could save both the trees and his heart; they save the orchard, forgive themselves, and begin again together.
about_author: Dominic Eriksen is a former orchard worker from the Pacific Northwest who writes quiet romances about people rebuilding what they thought was ruined. He lives beside an apple orchard older than his house and swears the trees keep better secrets than he does.

chapters.title: The Broken String
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Mid-concerto, his hand seizes and the performance collapses in front of a full hall. Flashbacks hint at old grief beneath the panic. Emotional beat: shame crystallizing into a vow never to feel that exposed again.

chapters.title: A Deed With Two Names
chapters.summary: Lior arrives at his grandmother's neglected orchard intending solitude, but the county clerk reveals a second name on the deed: Astrid Vane. His hands shake reading it. Emotional beat: the past arriving like weather he cannot outrun.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Gate
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She appears with her own copy of the deed and no apology, only practical talk of drainage and dead limbs. Their first argument ends with neither leaving. Emotional beat: anger masking relief that the other is real.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. They draft a brittle agreement: split the work, split the seasons, never discuss the past. A developer's letter arrives offering cash for the land. Emotional beat: a truce built on avoidance, already cracking.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Clearing storm damage, she finds the graft marks her grandmother taught Lior's grandmother to make decades ago—the families were entwined long before them. Emotional beat: wonder softening resentment.

chapters.title: Letters in the Root Cellar
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Behind a rotted shelf he discovers a tin of unsent letters in his grandmother's handwriting, addressed to Astrid's family. He reads only the first before stopping. Emotional beat: curiosity warring with self-protection.

chapters.title: Practice Without Music
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Unable to face the cello, he prunes instead, and Astrid quietly corrects his grip on the shears like a conductor. Their bodies remember cooperation before their words do. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Hearing Notice
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The county schedules a zoning hearing; the developer has filed to reclassify the orchard as commercial land. They have ninety days to prove active agricultural use or lose it. Emotional beat: shared enemy forging fragile alliance.

chapters.title: One Name, Spoken
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At a harvest fair, a mutual friend forces the question: why did Astrid leave? Lior lies smoothly and hates himself for it. Astrid overhears half. Emotional beat: loyalty to his own wound over the truth.

chapters.title: Blossom Frost
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A late frost threatens the blossoms; they work all night lighting smudge pots side by side, exhausted and laughing by dawn. Emotional beat: intimacy born of shared labor and near-loss.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He reads further into the tin: his grandmother begged Astrid's mother to let the young lovers stay together, and was refused for reasons redacted by torn pages. Emotional beat: the past revealing itself as more complicated than his grievance.

chapters.title: Interlude: Cello in the Barn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Astrid finds Lior playing at midnight, badly, bravely, and stays hidden rather than embarrass him. She leaves wildflowers on the barn rail. Emotional beat: love expressed through restraint.

chapters.title: The Rival Offer
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The developer makes Astrid a personal offer—enough to erase her debts—if she'll sell her half and testify the orchard is dormant. Emotional beat: survival pressing its thumb against loyalty.

chapters.title: Confession at the Well
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Astrid nearly tells him about the offer, then learns he lied at the fair. She confronts him; he admits he hid his breakdown from everyone, including her, years ago. Emotional beat: two silences colliding.

chapters.title: Torn Pages Found
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She matches the torn letter pages to papers her mother kept: Astrid left because her mother threatened to expose Lior's father's debts unless she went. Her sacrifice, not her betrayal. Emotional beat: grief reframing five lost years.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He learns what Astrid gave up and realizes his own invisibility was its own kind of cowardice. He signs nothing, says nothing yet—but begins practicing in daylight where she can hear. Emotional beat: forgiveness of the mirror beginning.

chapters.title: Deadline Week
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Preparing evidence of active cultivation, they inventory every tree, every graft, every letter. The developer escalates, questioning their co-ownership's validity. Emotional beat: urgency fusing them into a single team.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Both POVs interwoven. Astrid publicly declines the developer's money; Lior plays cello in the chamber—his first performance since the collapse—as testimony to the orchard's living purpose. Emotional beat: courage replacing concealment, climax of the external plot.

chapters.title: What I Never Said
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He gives Astrid the whole tin of letters and his own unwritten one spoken aloud: every year he loved her, every year he blamed her. Emotional beat: raw vulnerability, the emotional climax.

chapters.title: Grafting Season
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Spring: they graft new stock using both grandmothers' technique, formally renewing the deed as partners in every sense. Emotional beat: choice made freely, not out of debt or duty.

chapters.title: First Harvest Concert
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He performs among the trees for the town, hands steady, Astrid in the front row. The heart, he admits, was never containable—only waiting. Emotional beat: joy earned, the wound integrated.

chapters.title: Letters Worth Sending
chapters.summary: Shared closing POV. They mail the grandmother's letters at last, finishing sentences she left blank, and pin the deed to the barn wall with both names underlined. Emotional beat: peace—truth and love finally on the same page.
